newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia crudes mostly steady, paper Tapis firmer.
newsitem.headline: Asia crudes mostly steady, paper Tapis firmer.

text.p: Crude prices in Asia were mostly steady on Monday although paper Tapis was underpinned by a firmer bid.
October Tapis was bid in late trading at $22.20 versus Friday's bid of $21.90, which traders attributed to support for Tapis on a spread basis versus NYMEX crudes.

The Brent/Dubai for November was slightly weaker on Monday at $2.02/$2.07 from Friday's $2.05/$2.12 with December at $2.00/$2.10 versus -- the narrower intermonth spread reflecting the weakness of the Brent spreads.
Dubai intermonth spread stayed around recent levels with November/December and December/January indicated at 38/42 cents, just two cents wider than Friday's mid point of 40 cents.
However, paper traders said trading was quiet, partly hampered by a national holiday in Japan.
Brent/Dubai November paper traded at $2.04 on Friday between a trader and a state oil company.
Traders said a Murban deals between two majors was done at 21 cents over ADNOC. The deal could not be confirmed.
The last confirmed deals were at a premium of 19.5 cents.

Amid Indonesian grades, there was market talk of Minas trading at a premium of ICP plus 20 cents while at the same time a Japanese trader and refiner were said to have exchanged Minas at plus seven cents.
A producer sold late last week 200,000 barrels of Minas at plus 15 cents.
A 220,000 barrel cargo of Ardjuna was traded between a producer and China last week at ICP plus 30 cents a barrel.
